messages:
emily: heads-up — ACME reported p99 spikes on streaming endpoints after the runtime push ~08:10 UTC. Total end-to-end looks OK for most requests but initial byte (first-byte) is delayed for some streams (~800-1200ms). customer sample req ids: req-ACME-8981, req-ACME-8990. attaching quick repro below and a short trace excerpt.

matt: thanks. which model + backend variant are they hitting and are they using SSE or h2 streaming? any client pattern (long prompt vs short prompt)?

emily: model = redwood-openx-13b-8k, hosted runtime build = 2026-03-10-rc1, tenant = acme-corp. They use SSE in their browser product; typical prompts are short (~40 tokens) then streaming. Repro curl below.

emily: ```bash
# minimal repro (SSE)
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-openx-13b-8k","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
```

kai: I pulled the trace for req-ACME-8981 — trace shows stream-handler created, chunk generation begins quickly, but there's a 700-1100ms wait in transport.flush-coalesce before any bytes hit the wire. That aligns with first-byte delays but total time stays OK once flush happens.

alex: same trace shows the runtime emitted the first chunk at ~40ms, but our edge proxy coalescer is holding the packet to aggregate to 1s windows for that route. So source->runtime is fast, network/edge coalesce is the bottleneck.

matt: good catch. is this policy per-tenant or a global change? we need to avoid affecting high-throughput tenants.

jamie: coalesce window is a heuristic tuned for small chat workloads to reduce TLS/TCP overhead. It looks like the new runtime changed chunk boundary sizes (smaller chunks), which made the proxy heuristic wait longer. We can either: 1) reduce coalesce window for acme tenant only, or 2) make runtime produce slightly larger first chunk (prepend small "priming" token) as a temporary workaround.

emily: customer prefers no client changes. requesting per-tenant override.

matt: ok plan: short-term = per-tenant proxy flush override to 150ms; mid-term = adjust runtime to emit >=256B first chunk for streaming on that model; long-term = make coalesce heuristic consider model/chunk-size.

alex: to repro locally I ran the curl above and hit edge with `EDGE_COALESCE_MS=1000` -> first byte ~1.0s. with `EDGE_COALESCE_MS=150` -> first byte ~120ms. Logs:

```
[stream-handler] chunk_ready size=68 bytes at t=42ms
[edge-coalesce] holding buffer start t=42ms window_ms=1000
[edge-coalesce] flush -> send t=1042ms
```

matt: can ops apply tenant override? Jamie, any config name?

jamie: yes — route-level flag `edge.coalesce_ms` can be set per-tenant. value in ms. we'll set 150 for acme and monitor. command to apply via infra tooling: `infractl routes set acme-corp --set edge.coalesce_ms=150 --env prod` (needs infraops).

cw-deploy-bot: rollout scheduled by emily: infractl routes set acme-corp --set edge.coalesce_ms=150 --env prod (canary -> 5% -> 100%)

support-bot: escalation note added to ticket #SUP-2148, flagged as P1 streaming-ttfb.

matt: monitoring hooks we want: p50/p95/p99 first-byte, end-to-end total, and traces for any remaining p99. keep 5m resolution for first hour.

emily: override applied w/ canary at 5% at 08:45 UTC. rolling to 100% now. will paste metrics in a few mins.

emily: update — after full rollout p99 first-byte for acme dropped from ~1100ms -> ~180ms, p95 -> ~60ms. total times unchanged (good). customer confirmed noticeably faster UX. :tada:

matt: nice. next steps: 1) keep override for 24h while we validate no regressions; 2) create a runtime ticket to add a small first-chunk pad option or ensure chunk-size threshold; 3) add telemetry that correlates chunk size -> edge coalesce wait so we can alert when heuristics diverge. I'll own the postmortem.

kai: also add a short-term alert: if streaming-first-byte p99 increases >300ms over baseline for any tenant, create auto-rollout of per-tenant coalesce to 200ms as a protective fallback (needs SRE + infra automation).

jamie: filed infra change PR for per-tenant coalesce flag: PR#4821. runtime task created: RUNTIME-1298 (emit >=256B first-chunk option).

emily: customer notified and happy. leaving ticket open for postmortem and runtime fix. thanks team.

alex: one more note: let's avoid using global reductions to coalesce — increases cost. per-tenant is the low-cost fix.

matt: agreed. closing the urgent escalation, leaving follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
